assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, substrate-limited problem into a routine, general operation. Ligand design (bulky biaryl phosphines, hindered alkylphosphines) made the method broad and predictable. It is ubiquitous in medicinal chemistry and process chemistry and visible in countless syntheses, which is the kind of adoption I weigh most heavily.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic amination and the ligand classes that made it work, and both continued to expand scope for decades. Kosugi and Migita's tin-amide precursor chemistry is an important antecedent but the general, practical catalytic method is credited to the two. A two-person prize is clean.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of independent confirmation, industrial scale use and textbook status. Recognition is, if anything, overdue. The 2010 cross-coupling prize covers C-C coupling, so C-N is a distinct but related advance.
uncertainties: Committee may view this as an extension of the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize.
Relative priority of Kosugi (stannylamine antecedent) versus the two modern pioneers is a matter of interpretation; my recollection of the history is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Catalytic C-H functionalization, especially directing-group and ligand-controlled Pd chemistry, changed retrosynthetic thinking by allowing late-stage modification of otherwise inert bonds with predictable site selectivity. Strong fit with efficiency in synthesis: fewer steps, no prefunctionalization. Impact on total synthesis and drug discovery is large and growing.
assessment.attribution: Yu's ligand-enabled, template-controlled meta/para and sp3 C-H activation and Sanford's Pd(II)/Pd(IV) and fluorination/oxidative chemistry are distinct decisive contributions. Hartwig (borylation) and Daugulis (directing groups) are also important, and the field is broad, so a three-person cap forces hard choices. I propose the two with the most general, widely adopted platforms.
assessment.maturity: Methods are widely used but scope and robustness are still maturing; practical industrial adoption is partial compared with cross-coupling. Recognition is plausible now but could reasonably wait.
uncertainties: Overlap with Hartwig, who is also credited under B016, and the very broad field make fair credit contested.
Whether C-H functionalization is conceptually one discovery or several related ones.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a vast mode of radical and single-electron reactivity under mild conditions using simple light sources, and it is now routine in discovery chemistry labs and increasingly in flow and process settings. The conceptual simplification of hard radical transformations is exactly the type of change I value.
assessment.attribution: The 2008 to 2009 reports from Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz (with MacMillan) launched the synthetic field; Melchiorre, Konig and Fukuzumi provided related photochemistry. MacMillan is already a laureate (2021), which complicates the configuration, so I leave him out and propose three others; this is a judgment, and the credit among many contributors is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted with strong independent confirmation, though the field is young enough that the most durable applications are still emerging. Timing is acceptable but not urgent.
uncertainties: Prior MacMillan prize and the many co-founders make allocation contested.
Mechanistic details of some reported reactions remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically hindered acid-base pairs can heterolytically activate H2 and other small molecules without metals, a clear conceptual novelty with downstream use in metal-free hydrogenation. The idea is simple and chemically new, though practical impact so far is narrower than for cross-coupling.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 metal-free H2 activation is the founding report and Erker developed the field extensively and the reactivity of related systems. Both are clearly decisive and a two-person prize is natural.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across many groups; applications in synthesis and catalysis are still limited, making the timing slightly early on impact grounds.
uncertainties: Whether conceptual novelty alone suffices without a broadly used method.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes (imidazolylidenes and the earlier phosphinocarbene) overturned the view that such species were only transient. N-heterocyclic carbenes became ubiquitous ligands and organocatalysts, enabling robust metathesis and cross-coupling catalysts.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand's 1988 stable phosphinocarbene and Arduengo's 1991 crystalline NHC are the decisive founding isolations. Nolan, Rovis and Bode contributed to applications but are not the core of the original discovery. Two is a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades of confirmed impact and wide use; the discovery is mature and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Credit ordering between Bertrand and Arduengo for the foundational isolation is sometimes debated.
The practical impact is mostly via downstream catalysts, which may blur the prize's focus.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new chemical modality that hijacks E3 ligases to eliminate proteins, with clinical candidates. I ask what was new chemically: heterobifunctional design and ligand discovery for cereblon and VHL are real molecular design advances, though the biology contribution is large.
assessment.attribution: Crews originated the PROTAC concept, Ciulli developed VHL ligands and degrader design principles, and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Deshaies, Gray, Ito, Sakamoto and Kim are also credited, so allocation is crowded and uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still emerging; independent confirmation of the mechanism is strong, but therapeutic maturity is partial. Slightly early.
uncertainties: Many credible contributors; fair three-person split is difficult.
Border with biology and medicine; clinical outcomes not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: ATRP provided a general, robust route to well-defined polymers with controlled architecture using transition metal catalysis, a method widely used in materials science. It is conceptually a clean bond-forming control strategy with large practical adoption.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski, with Wang, and Sawamoto independently reported the metal-catalyzed controlled radical polymerization in 1995. Kamigaito is a co-author with Sawamoto, but I would limit to the three principal names; the Wang and Matyjaszewski pairing versus Sawamoto's independent work needs care.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely adopted over three decades; timing is fine though its competitor RAFT is similarly important.
uncertainties: Relationship with RAFT (B053) and nitroxide-mediated polymerization may complicate a single prize.
Polymer chemistry is less central to my own expertise, so I defer to colleagues on relative impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The phosphoramidite method made routine automated DNA synthesis possible and underpins PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide therapeutics. Methodologically it is a clear case of a reliable chemical step that enabled much of molecular biology.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite coupling chemistry; Hood is credited for instrumentation and automation, whose chemical novelty is smaller. I propose Caruthers alone and acknowledge that this leaves out the automation contribution.
assessment.maturity: Foundational since the early 1980s and thoroughly confirmed, but recognition is arguably long delayed and the field has had decades of previous opportunity; possibly a candidate that passed its moment.
uncertainties: Age and timing of the principal contributor.
Others (Letsinger, Beaucage) may deserve credit but are not in the supplied names.
